title: Cap. VIII: Remote cause yes; deny inhering sin or drop immediate imputation
pass_a_gloss: Second cut: Placeus distinguishes the phrase "on account of" the same way he did earlier. It can name a remote cause or a proximate cause. If remote, he grants Garissoles the whole argument; if proximate, he refuses the premise. Reason repeated often: Adam's first actual sin causes our inhering sin, and our inhering sin causes death; whatever causes a cause also causes that cause's effect. Hinge: either join Pelagius, Pighius, and Socinus in denying inhering sin and its guilt, or you cannot squeeze out of the Apostle's wording an antecedent / immediate imputation of Adam's actual sin. Stops before the verse-19 head.
pass_b_english: Next I distinguish "on account of" as above. It marks either a remote cause or a proximate one. If the remote, the whole argument is granted; if the proximate, the premise is denied. For, as I have driven home many times, Adam's first actual sin is the cause of our inhering sin, and this is the cause of death; and what is the cause of a cause is also the cause of the effect. Either, with Pelagius, Pighius, and Socinus, inhering sin and its guilt must be denied, or it is impossible from the Apostle's words to force an antecedent or immediate imputation of Adam's actual sin.
source_text: Deinde distinguo propter ut supra. Nam vel causam remotam designat, vel proximam. Si illam, conceditur totum argumentum; si hanc, negatur propositio. Est enim, ut multoties inculcavi, primum Adami peccatum actuale causa nostri peccati inhaerentis, & hoc causa mortis: quod autem est causa causae, id causa est etiam effectus. Aut cum Pelagio, Pighio, & Socino negandum est peccatum inhaerens ejusque reatus, aut impossibile est ex verbis Apostoli imputationem peccati Adae actualis antecedentem seu immediatam efficere.
